newsitem.title: UK: DLR SPIKES UP THEN RECEDES AFTER STEADY BUBA REPO.
newsitem.headline: DLR SPIKES UP THEN RECEDES AFTER STEADY BUBA REPO.

text.p: The dollar initially rose half a pfennig after the Bundesbank kept its repo rate steady at a fixed 3.00 percent but shed its gains as the threat of rising German rates remained in the market, analysts said.

The Bundesbank did not comment further after it set its weekly repo rate. Though speculation about a repo move had receded in recent days, dealers still held back before the annoucement and then bought dollars on the news.
"Nothing has changed. The threat that the Bundesbank will send a tightening signal to the market is still there," said Joe Prendergast, head of foreign exchange research at CSFB.
At 0745 GMT the dollar was at 1.8605/15 marks compared with 1.8545/55 in late European trading on Monday but more than half a pfennig below its high after the repo announcement.

Dealers said speculation about what the Bundesbank would do at next week's tender was kept alive because the central bank announced only one fortnightly tender this week. Firm resistance in the 1.8680 to 1.8715 zone also prompted the dollar to go into reverse.
Prendergast said attention had shifted from its focus on German rates to the near-term direction of U.S. asset markets after Friday's sharp fall. Asset markets recovered on Monday.

Tim Fox, chief treasury economist at Standard Chartered, said the expected continuation of a fixed rate was bearish for the mark. Concern voiced recently by Bundesbankers about the weakness of the mark had spurred the market into thinking that the central bank would allow the repo rate to edge higher even though speculation about a move had receded in the past days.
"Adjusting interest rates in order to influence the exchange rate is out of character for the Bundesbank," said Fox. A continued fixed rate would be bearish for the mark, he said.
The focus for the forex market is now on the Treasury market's reaction to this week's U.S. data.
